text:
tara: Heads-up — seeing runner heartbeat throttling during nightly evals, dashboard drilldowns lagging and CI jobs flickering to queued then succeeded with no samples showing. :eyes:

mike: Can you paste the runner logs?

tara: pasted minimal excerpt below, happened across 3 runs starting ~23:04 UTC

```
2026-03-18T23:04:12Z runner[worker-7]: heartbeat=delayed; last_ack=120s ago; inflight=32
2026-03-18T23:04:13Z autoscaler: throttle_scale_down=true reason=budget_pressure
2026-03-18T23:04:13Z kv-cache: miss_ratio=0.42
2026-03-18T23:04:14Z runner[worker-7]: mark job xfer queued -> ack
2026-03-18T23:04:14Z dashboard-ingest: batch_write timeout 5s
```

sofia: Hmm throttle_scale_down=true during busy window sounds wrong — shouldn't scale down mid-batch. Did we flip any budgets?

minh: I saw a similar spike last week when HPA CPU metrics had a gap due to node exporter restart. Can you check pod restarts? `kubectl get pods -n eval -o wide --field-selector=status.phase!=Running`

mike: Also check the runner heartbeat config: `runner.config.heartbeat_interval` — if it's too low the monitor marks delays more aggressively.

tara: Pod restarts are low (<1), but node-level OOM was present on one host. Attaching k8s event snippet:

```
Events:
  Type     Reason     Age   From               Message
  ----     ------     ----  ----               -------
  Warning  OOMKilled  23m   kubelet, ip-10-0  Container killed due to memory usage
```

sofia: If a node OOM happens, autoscaler could misinterpret capacity and throttle. But dashboard-ingest timeout indicates backpressure upstream too.

minh: Quick workaround: bump runner.heartbeat_grace to 180s for nightly evals and increase dashboard-ingest write timeout to 15s in config map. That should reduce false positives while we root cause.

tara: Will try the config change on staging first. Deploy command I'm using:

```
kubectl apply -f k8s/overlays/staging/runner-config.yaml
kubectl rollout restart deployment/runner -n eval
```

mike: After that, let's run a smoke job: `./ci/tools/run_eval_smoke.sh --samples 100 --model rdx-open-3b` and watch the console for queued->ack transitions.

tara: Ran staging change. Initial smoke shows no heartbeat delays yet, dashboard ingest writes seem stable. Jobs now show steady progress. :thumbsup:

sofia: Good. For root cause we should correlate node OOMs with autoscaler decisions and controller logs around the times. Putting together a short postmortem plan: 1) timeline from metrics (node, pod, autoscaler, runner) 2) reproduce in perf env with induced low-memory node 3) fix autoscaler policy to avoid scale-down during high backlog 4) make ingest writes idempotent/queued to tolerate timeouts.

mike: Agree. Also add an alert rule: if heartbeat_delay > 60s AND ingest_write_errors > 0 fire a P1 for oncall.

eval-bot: Test run 2026-03-19T00:12:00Z: smoke eval passed, 100 samples completed, avg latency ok.

tara: Thanks all — I'll file a short ticket with the timeline and link to logs and the staging run. Posting logs + smoke run link here: https://redwood-internal/perf/runs/2376543219-smoke1

minh: Thanks — ping me on the ticket if you want me to simulate OOM in perf.

sofia: Nice catch. Let's keep an eye on nightly run tomorrow.

tara: Will follow up after tomorrow's run and attach postmortem draft. :memo:
